nearestUnrefutedMisses.equivalentReplacementExists: yes - [...new Set(list)] has identical first-occurrence order and identity semantics for string elements
nearestUnrefutedMisses.whyNotShipped: below the 5% bar on its own, and it is the only part of the memory.js share that is provably equivalent without caching.

acceptanceRuleThatWouldHaveApplied.writtenWhen: after the first pass attribution (§3.1/§3.2) and before any candidate was selected; no candidate ever entered it in either pass, so no measurement was produced under it and the rule text itself was not revised when this record was rewritten for the final tree
acceptanceRuleThatWouldHaveApplied.text: Ship if and only if ALL of the following hold on the real official backend, with alternating A/B on the same load and the baseline side rebuilt by applying a byte-exact inverse of the patch in a scratch copy: (1) end-to-end wall-clock gain >= 3% with non-overlapping per-round intervals; (2) the A/B difference exceeds the same-code A/A control drift measured in the same session; (3) peak RSS and heap are not worse; (4) semantic equivalence proven by differential comparison of every durable byte plus at least one adversarial counterexample designed to break the candidate. Otherwise restore lib/ byte-identically and record the withdrawal with its counterexample.
acceptanceRuleThatWouldHaveApplied.verdict: NOT TRIGGERED, in this pass as in the previous one: no candidate reached the plausibility screen. Production code unchanged; lib/ byte-identical (41 file digests and the git diff -- lib/ digest are the same before and after the pass).

unmeasured: The write shape where the transaction actually appends to an active archive (files.length > 0, syncStage + installArchiveFiles + 3 fsyncs). Neither prescribed load produces it in either pass; archive-stage-io.md measured it on the pre-f89221f code, so its current per-transaction cost has not been re-derived.
The official JsonStorageBackend's own durability calls (fs.promises handle sync) are inside the wall clock and appear as native rename/open/fsync in the profile, but are not itemised separately.
Physical disk bytes written, cold page cache, non-APFS filesystems, other platforms.
Production arrival distribution: how often a real agent step carries 0 vs 1 vs N new events, and how often a real archive transaction changes a file. Every share here is conditional on the fixture.
Peak RSS was not measured in either pass; nothing was shipped, so there is no memory claim either way.
The measurement tree is a working tree (HEAD plus uncommitted changes to four files), not a commit. The numbers describe that working tree only.
